context:
Goal: a plain "use Opus" message grants Opus only to the work your nearby messages name (your 226 b).
What this is: when you type "use opus" with no time and no role, a hook asks a model which work your messages name, and Opus covers only that work. Example: you write "fix the map lint", then "use opus": Opus covers the map-lint lane only.
- a (main today, since #1244): the hook reads the messages you sent before "use opus". One model read, at the ask.
- b: the hook also reads each message you send after it, while the grant lives. A later "also the waiting page" or "only the tests" changes what Opus covers. One model read on each of your messages, even ones that never mention Opus.
Problem (money): b adds a model call to each of your messages while a grant lives.
Based on (ruling): 226 b: the scope comes from your nearby messages.
Based on (ruling): 256 none (11:22 CST Nov 6): "i dont understand my two options here". Asked again with this explanation.
Based on (read): #1244 (batch 10, Nov 5 06:36 CST) put a on main: hooks/local_time.py reads your earlier messages with the ask.
Departs from: main (earlier messages only) — b also lets a later message change a live grant.

short: Opus ask: read later messages too?
title: Should a plain Opus ask also read your messages after the ask?
why: It keeps the cost to one call per ask, and the part both options need is already being built.
